name: Benign Colorectal Diseases: Diverticulitis, Ulcerative Colitis, and Volvulus

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / ASCRS Clinical Practice Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Hinchey classification stratifies acute diverticulitis from Stage I (pericolic abscess) to Stage IV (feculent peritonitis)
Uncomplicated acute diverticulitis is managed conservatively, whereas purulent or feculent peritonitis mandates emergency Hartmann procedure or resection with diverting loop ileostomy
Restorative proctocolectomy with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) is the curative surgical procedure of choice for medically refractory ulcerative colitis
Sigmoid volvulus displays a characteristic coffee-bean sign pointing to the right upper quadrant and is initially decompressed via rigid sigmoidoscopy
Cecal volvulus represents true axial twist of a mobile right colon, requiring emergency right hemicolectomy rather than endoscopic decompression
reference.pathophysiology: Colonic diverticula represent false pulsion diverticula (herniation of mucosa and submucosa through gaps in muscularis propria where nutrient vessels penetrate). Micro-perforation caused by fecalith obstruction incites localized pericolic inflammation, which may progress to walled-off abscesses, purulent peritonitis, or free fecal contamination. In ulcerative colitis, diffuse mucosal inflammation of the colon and rectum causes bloody diarrhea, tenesmus, and in severe cases, transmural toxic megacolon characterized by colonic dilation (>6 cm) and impending perforation.
additionalDifferentials: Acute sigmoid diverticulitis versus perforating sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma
Toxic megacolon in ulcerative colitis versus Clostridioides difficile pseudomembranous colitis
Sigmoid volvulus versus acute mechanical large bowel obstruction from left-sided neoplasm
Ischemic colitis of the splenic flexure (Griffiths point) versus infectious colitis
additionalInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT (gold standard for acute diverticulitis staging and abscess localization)
Plain abdominal radiography demonstrating marked colonic distention in toxic megacolon or volvulus
Endoscopic inspection of rectal stump and pouchoscopy for post-operative pouchitis monitoring
Serial abdominal examinations and inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein and procalcitonin)
